content: The use of ofloxacin has been studied for the syndromic management of sexually transmitted infections in resource-limited settings, as reported in the Journal of Antimicrobial Chemotherapy in 2002. Sands M. explored the treatment of anorectal gonorrhea infections in men in a 1980 study published in JAMA. Schumacher CM and Ghanem KG compared retreatment rates for uncomplicated gonorrhea using ceftriaxone and azithromycin versus ceftriaxone and doxycycline in a 2013 study in Sexually Transmitted Diseases. Shams-ur-Rehman et al. evaluated the clinical efficacy of various drugs for treating gonorrhea in a 2009 study in the Journal of Ayub Medical College Abbottabad. Shi DQ compared the clinical efficacy of sparfloxacin and spectinomycin for gonorrhea treatment in a 2000 study published in the Chinese Journal of Antibiotics. Handsfield HH and colleagues conducted a multicenter trial comparing fleroxacin and ceftriaxone for treating uncomplicated gonorrhea, published in the American Journal of Medicine in 1993. Stapinski A and Gede K reported on the treatment of gonorrhea with spectinomycin in a 1986 study in Przeglad Dermatologiczny. Steingrimsson O and colleagues evaluated azithromycin for treating sexually transmitted diseases in a 1990 study in the Journal of Antimicrobial Chemotherapy. They also studied single-dose azithromycin for treating gonorrhea and infections caused by Chlamydia trachomatis and Ureaplasma urealyticum in men, as published in Sexually Transmitted Diseases in 1994. Stratigos JD et al. examined the use of spectinomycin hydrochloride for gonorrhea treatment in a 1973 study in the British Journal of Venereal Diseases. Swanson WH and colleagues assessed single-dose azithromycin therapy for Neisseria gonorrhoeae and Chlamydia trachomatis in a 2001 study in the West Indian Medical Journal. Takahashi S et al. evaluated the efficacy of a single 2-gram dose of azithromycin extended-release for male urethritis in a 2014 study in Antibiotics. Tian HQ and Dong LY studied ceftriaxone in treating 115 gonorrhea patients in a 2002 study in the Chinese Journal of New Drugs and Clinical Remedies. Tupasi TE and colleagues compared cefuroxime, thiamphenicol, spectinomycin, and penicillin G for treating uncomplicated infections caused by penicillinase-producing strains of Neisseria gonorrhoeae in a 1983 study in the British Journal of Venereal Diseases. They also conducted a comparative trial of thiamphenicol, penicillin, and spectinomycin for gonococcal infections in a 1984 study in Sexually Transmitted Diseases. Another study by Tupasi et al. in 1982 compared spectinomycin, cefuroxime, thiamphenicol, and penicillin G for treating gonococcal infections in women, published in the Journal of Infectious Diseases. Turanova EN and colleagues conducted a clinical-laboratory study on the effectiveness of kanamycin for treating gonorrhea in women, published in Vestnik Dermatologii i Venerologii in 1975. Tuz F and Hatos G studied spectinomycin hydrochloride for male urethral gonorrhea treatment in a 1973 study in the Medical Journal of Australia. Verdon MS et al. evaluated single-dose cefixime for treating uncomplicated gonorrhea in a 1993 study in Sexually Transmitted Diseases. Waugh MA conducted an open study on the safety and efficacy of a single oral dose of azithromycin for treating uncomplicated gonorrhea in men and women, published in the Journal of Antimicrobial Chemotherapy in 1993. Willcox RR studied spectinomycin for treating gonorrhea in males in a 1974 study in the British Journal of Venereal Diseases. Wójtowicz U et al. reported on the incidence and treatment outcomes of beta-lactamase-positive gonorrhea with spectinomycin in a 1990 study in Przeglad Dermatologiczny. Yoon JY and colleagues compared kanamycin and gentamicin for treating uncomplicated male gonococcal urethritis in a 1988 study in the Korean Journal of Dermatology. Zajdowicz TR et al. compared ceftriaxone and cefoxitin for treating penicillin-resistant gonococcal urethritis in a 1983 study in the British Journal of Venereal Diseases. Zhou YS and colleagues observed the clinical effects of etimicin sulfate and spectinomycin for gonorrhea treatment in a 2000 study in the Chinese Journal of Antibiotics. The WHO guidelines for treating Neisseria gonorrhoeae emphasize the importance of dual therapy over single therapy, particularly in light of emerging antimicrobial resistance. Dual therapy typically includes ceftriaxone plus azithromycin or cefixime plus azithromycin. Single therapy is only recommended when local resistance data confirm susceptibility. The guidelines highlight the challenges of treating oropharyngeal gonococcal infections due to their role as reservoirs for resistance genes and their potential for sustained transmission. The evidence supporting these recommendations is of very low quality, but dual therapy is favored due to its higher efficacy and the global rise in resistance to single therapies.
